papers.title: A posteriori estimates for inverse evolutionary problems
papers.abstract: The paper is focused on a posteriori error analysis of evolutionary problems, which are ill-posed in the sense of Hadamard. They may have no solutions and respective approximations may be highly unstable. For these problems, the a posteriori error estimation concept applicable to well-posed problems is not valid and requires a significant reformulation. A posteriori estimates of the functional type provide the basis for addressing this issue. They generate computable quantities that estimate the distance between a function (approximate solution to the inverse problem) and exact solution of a "close" well-posed initial boundary value problem associated with the same differential equation. The solution of this close problem exactly satisfies one part of the imposed conditions and the others are satisfied approximately with the accuracy $\eps$. This idea is elaborated for several evolutionary problems generated by the reaction-convection-diffusion equation: backward parabolic problem, problem with non-local time conditions, Cauchy parabolic problem, and parameter(s) identification problem. The estimates derived not only control the accuracy of approximate solutions, but also suggest a unified approach to calculating them numerically.

papers.title: Inverse scattering for the one-dimensional discrete Schr\"odinger operator: a computational perspective
papers.abstract: We revisit inverse scattering for the one-dimensional discrete Schr\"odinger operator with compactly supported perturbation. We consider a computational perspective, adapted to the case of a digitally sampled reflection coefficient, to determine the perturbation in the form of a Jacobi matrix, including a computation of the length of the smallest interval supporting the perturbation. A new representation of scattering data in terms of orthogonal polynomials underpins the computational results. A key technical role is played by polynomials on the circle constructed from pairs of successive orthogonal polynomials on the line. The inverse algorithm is demonstrated on numerical examples.

papers.title: Convex Structure-Preserving EDMD: Passive Koopman Matrices as $Q$-Contractions
papers.abstract: Extended dynamic mode decomposition (EDMD) approximates the Koopman operator using a matrix based on a finite set of observables. However, the least-squares matrix of a port-Hamiltonian (pH) system is generally neither passive nor invariant-preserving. We demonstrate that the implicit midpoint discretization of a lifted pH model precisely preserves energy balance, passivity, and all linear Casimirs for every step size. For a fixed storage metric $Q$, the resulting Koopman matrices are the Cayley transforms of $(J-R)Q$, where $J$ is skew-symmetric and $R$ is positive semidefinite. This set does not depend on the step size and is the closure of all Q-contractions. This set is LMI-representable; therefore, structure-preserving EDMD, including ports through a discrete-time Kalman-Yakubovich-Popov condition and Casimirs through affine constraints, is a semidefinite program. The constrained estimate is a projection of the unconstrained estimate in the data-weighted norm and cannot increase estimation error when the population target is pH-compatible. For every $Q$-contraction, a certified bound on the lifted prediction error grows linearly at most in time, whereas it grows geometrically for unconstrained models with Q-gain above one. Benchmarks on a damped pendulum and a damped rigid body demonstrate that constrained models never generate energy and that imposed Casimirs are maintained with solver accuracy (approximately $10^{-8}$). In contrast, EDMD may diverge or lose the Casimir with noisy data. The benchmarks also demonstrate that when $Q$ is the physical energy, the constrained models are less accurate than EDMD and can exhibit significant structural bias.

papers.title: Moonshine Conjecture Formalized
papers.abstract: The celebrated and intimidating Moonshine Conjecture has now been formalized in Lean. This achievement might suggest that, once a sufficiently large library compiles, the principal mathematical work is complete. This paper tells a less optimistic story. During our formalization project, we repeatedly encountered two problems that a formally checked proof alone does not settle: (1) whether the formal statements actually express the mathematics we humans expect, and (2) how that meaning survives as the repositories and their dependencies evolve. We argue that there is no magic pill that turns a large agent-produced library into mathematics a community can trust. Even after the proofs are checked by the Lean kernel, someone must judge whether the definitions and statements express the intended mathematics and whether future updates preserve that meaning. This work, even when done, can only be trusted. We must therefore return to the usual trust model: relying on the mathematical judgment of maintainers and expert communities. But semantic review is expensive, making it tempting to keep producing code and take successful kernel checks as sufficient grounds for trust. This shortcut accumulates semantic debt: definitions and results with unchecked mathematical interpretations are reused as foundations for further work. A library may keep compiling and produce the desired formal theorem while users lose track of which mathematical claims they can responsibly rely on. Reliable reuse is also a prerequisite for Terence Tao's vision of formal mathematics as something people can navigate, explain, learn from, and build with. This paper takes our work connecting the VOA and CFSG repositories for the Moonshine Conjecture as a case study of the challenges of reliable reuse as formal developments scale.

papers.title: Scattering by two parallel semi--infinite arrays of sound--soft scatterers
papers.abstract: This article considers the scattering of an acoustic wave by two identical semi--infinite arrays of point scatterers which are positioned parallel to one another. The resulting system of scattering coefficients is formulated as a pair of coupled discrete Wiener--Hopf equations with a full $2\times2$ matrix kernel composed of two scalar kernel functions that represent interaction within the selected array and between the two arrays. Exploiting the symmetry of the two arrays, we introduce symmetric and antisymmetric components of the scattering coefficients, which decouple the matrix Wiener--Hopf system into two independent scalar problems with kernels given by the sum and difference of the two original kernel functions. The scalar Wiener--Hopf equations are then solved using the Wiener--Hopf technique in a very similar way to what has previously been used to solve the semi--infinite array problem. The original definitions of the two scalar kernels are represented by a lattice sum and practical evaluation techniques are discussed. Comparisons with previous work are also critically discussed. The resulting formulation provides an exact analytical solution to a coupled semi--infinite array problem and illustrates how symmetry can reduce a discrete matrix Wiener--Hopf problem to two scalar problems.

papers.title: Tackling Many-Body Coulomb Singularity by Randomization
papers.abstract: Many-body Coulomb dynamics is central to quantum chemistry and molecular simulation, yet the Coulomb singularity undermines both the standard error analysis and performance of product formulas. Even for the simple hydrogen ground state, the celebrated Trotter formulas converge more slowly than their nominal order, and going to higher order does not help. Randomization by itself does not resolve this. We show that conventional qDRIFT suffers the same loss of accuracy, and that for general initial states, the errors of both Trotter formulas and qDRIFT can decrease more slowly than any power of the number of time steps (logarithmically). To overcome these limitations, we introduce supersmoothing qDRIFT, a randomized product formula that turns a physical property of free particle propagation into an algorithmic resource. Our algorithm achieves an error bound that decreases linearly with the time step, uniformly over \textit{all} initial states and without any smoothness or energy assumptions. Combined with spatial discretization analysis, the resulting end-to-end gate count improves on those of qubitization and high-order Trotter formulas applied directly to the discretized Hamiltonian, despite first-order convergence in time. This work demonstrates new ways of utilizing continuum dynamics to achieve algorithmic advantage.

papers.title: Symmetry, boundary conditions, and the Noether correspondence of the Zakharov--Kuznetsov equation
papers.abstract: Conserved quantities of nonlinear dispersive wave equations are typically derived on the whole plane, whereas numerical simulations evaluate them on a torus. We examine how compactifying one or both spatial directions affects the Noether correspondences of the Zakharov--Kuznetsov equation, obtained from its potential Lagrangian, on the family of domains $\{\mathbb{R},\mathbb{T}\}^2$. The outcome is a three-valued classification: intrinsic, chart-dependent, or defective. Only the two first moments, whose characteristics carry an undifferentiated coordinate weight, are affected. A moment can become defective only if its weighted direction is compact and the mass flux crosses the seam of the chosen fundamental domain; for the Zakharov--Kuznetsov equation this happens exactly for the longitudinal moment when $x$ is compact. The status of each moment depends only on the boundary condition along its weighted direction. When $x$ is compact, the Galilean boost still maps solutions to solutions, but no global Noether charge corresponds to it.

papers.title: Eigenvalues and Resonances of the Kramers-Fokker-Planck Operator in the Large-Friction Limit
papers.abstract: We study the eigenvalues and resonances of the Kramers-Fokker-Planck operator by the methods of analytic dilation and phase-space deformation. We prove that in the large-friction limit $\gamma\to+\infty$, there are neither eigenvalues nor resonances away from the thresholds $\gamma N$, and that near each threshold $\gamma k$, there exists a bijection between the eigenvalues and resonances of the Kramers-Fokker-Planck operator and those of the Witten Laplacian at the level $k$, $-\Delta_V^{(k)}=-\Delta_V\otimes 1_{\mu_k}-d\Gamma_k(\operatorname{Hess}V)$. We also show that each negative eigenvalue of $-\Delta_V^{(k)}$, $k\geq 1$, produces a pole of the resolvent at distance of order $\gamma^{-1}$ below $\gamma k$, whose imaginary part is $O(e^{-c\gamma})$ for every $c<2\delta_V$. Here $\delta_V$ is the width of a strip of analyticity of $V$.

papers.title: The regular $N$-gon maximizes first positive Neumann eigenvalue among simple polygons with at most $N$ sides and fixed area
papers.abstract: Let $\Phi(P)=|P|\mu_1(P)$, where $\mu_1(P)$ is the first positive Neumann eigenvalue of $P$. For every $N\ge3$, the regular $N$-gon $R_N$ uniquely maximizes $\Phi$, up to congruence, among simple polygons of fixed area with at most $N$ sides. The values $\Phi(R_N)$ increase strictly with $N$. The maximization theorem answers Laugesen's question \cite[Problem~(1), p.~405]{ABLW} and proves the polygonal Szeg\H{o}--Weinberger conjecture of Laugesen and Siudeja \cite[Conjecture~6.36]{LSH}. It also implies that the triangular lattice maximizes the first positive Neumann eigenvalue of the Voronoi cell at fixed covolume.

papers.title: Nonlinear stability of periodic waves in the Benjamin-Ono equation
papers.abstract: We construct the Lyapunov functional for the periodic waves of the Benjamin-Ono equation based on the conservation of momentum, energy, and a higher-order energy, which exists due to integrability. Positivity of the second variation of the Lyapunov functional for perturbations in Sobolev space $H^1(\mathbb{R})$ is established by utilizing the basis properties of eigenfunctions of the linearized Benjamin-Ono equation in $L^2(\mathbb{R})$. Coercivity of the Lyapunov functional for co-periodic and multiple-periodic perturbations yields the nonlinear orbital stability of the periodic waves in the periodic domain.

papers.title: Projectivized ASEP-Bethe system and counting solutions
papers.abstract: This paper addresses the problem of counting solutions to the ASEP-Bethe ansatz equations. In an earlier preprint, Brattain, Do, and Saenz presented an algebro-geometric method for counting the number of such solutions. As their method relies on sophisticated machinery, it requires advanced knowledge of algebraic geometry and topology. In this paper, we provide an alternative and simpler method for counting solutions, based on a standard intersection theory on projective varieties. We take a conventional approach in algebraic geometry: ``Projectivize the problem and count degrees.'' We introduce a projectivized version of the ASEP-Bethe equations, whose solution set is realized as a subscheme of a certain projective variety. Varying the hopping-rate parameter $p$, we give a one-parameter family $S$ of the solution sets. We show that, for the ASEP with $n$ sites and $m$ particles, the fiber $S|_p$ with generic $p$ contains $\binom{n}{m}$ points with multiplicity, which equals the expected number of admissible Bethe roots to the ASEP-Bethe ansatz equation.

papers.title: Well-posedness and finite-time breakdown for Euler-alignment systems with diffusive chemotaxis
papers.abstract: We investigate a recent class of pressureless Euler systems arising in biological contexts, in which the velocity evolution is driven, besides the nonlocal alignment interaction, by the gradient of a concentration self-produced by the population. We first establish local existence and uniqueness of strong solutions, in a class requiring no spatial derivative of the initial population density, together with a continuation criterion. We then derive sufficient conditions on the initial data for finite-time breakdown in the multidimensional setting, with an explicit upper bound for the maximal time of existence. Numerical simulations complement the analysis and illustrate the transition between regular and singular regimes, and the role of the chemotactic strength in the onset of blow-up.

papers.title: Algebraic dark solitons versus rogue waves in the massive Thirring model
papers.abstract: We address the existence of algebraically decaying solitary waves on the nonzero wave background in the massive Thirring model (MTM) in laboratory coordinates. We find the precise condition of the spectral stability and instability of the nonzero wave background. In the case of instability, we distinguish modulational, side-band, and full-band instabilities and show that the rogue wave exists if and only if the nonzero wave background is modulationally unstable. For the other unstable cases and in the case of stability, we show that there exist exactly two algebraic dark solitons which correspond to the end points in the admissible range of the wave speed for the dark soliton propagation.

papers.title: Brane Tilings and Polygons with Two Interior Points
papers.abstract: We fully classify the brane tilings and the 4d N=1 supersymmetric quiver gauge theories corresponding to toric Calabi-Yau 3-folds whose toric diagrams are convex lattice polygons with two interior lattice points. There are 45 such polygons up to GL(2,Z) transformations and lattice translations: 5 triangles, 19 quadrilaterals, 16 pentagons and 5 hexagons. We identify all 323 toric phases corresponding to these toric Calabi-Yau 3-folds. For every toric phase, we present the brane tiling with its quiver and superpotential, the perfect matching matrix and the F- and D-term charge matrices. For each brane tiling, we study the mesonic moduli space of the corresponding abelian 4d N=1 theory through its Hilbert series and plethystic logarithm, and identify its generators and their leading relations. We also identify the mesonic global symmetry for each brane tiling and determine the superconformal U(1)R charges.

papers.title: Reduction by stages for affine W-algebras
papers.abstract: Given a pair of nilpotent orbits in a simple Lie algebra, one can associate a pair of vertex algebras called affine W-algebras. Under some compatibility conditions on these orbits, we prove that one of these W-algebras can be obtained as the quantum Hamiltonian reduction of the other. This property is called reduction by stages. We provide several examples in classical and exceptional types. To prove reduction by stages for affine W-algebras, we use our previous work on reduction by stages for the Slodowy slices associated with these nilpotent orbits, these slices being the associated varieties of the W-algebras. We also prove and use the fact that each W-algebra can be defined using several equivalent BRST cohomology constructions: choosing the right BRST complexes allows us to connect the two W-algebras in a natural way.

papers.title: Conformally flat Mercator equation and conserved quantities of conformal circles
papers.abstract: We study properties of solutions of the conformal Mercator equation on the conformal sphere. We focus on conformal circles and give two different approaches of finding their conserved quantities from conformal Killing vector fields - variational and tractorial. We find a direct relation between the two sets of quantities.

papers.title: Submanifolds, restriction of differential operators and Schouten-Nijenhuis bracket
papers.abstract: In this article, we present new formulas for restricting the Hodge operator, the codifferential and the Hodge Laplacian to a submanifold. These formulas are concise, thanks to the use of tools for differential forms (Schouten-Nijenhuis bracket and generalized interior product). They also facilitate explicit calculations for practical applications.

papers.title: Characterisation of Markov property on planar maps
papers.abstract: We revisit, in a self contained way, the Markov property on planar maps and decorated planar maps from three perspectives. First, we characterize the laws on these planar maps that satisfy both the Markov property and rerooting invariance, showing that they are Boltzmann-type maps. Second, we provide a comprehensive characterization of random submaps, that we call stopping maps, satisfying the Markov property, demonstrating that they are not restricted to those obtained through a peeling procedure. Third, we introduce decorated metric planar maps in which edges are replaced by copies of random length intervals $[0,w_e]$, and the decorations are given by continuous functions on the edges. We define a probability measure on them that is the analogue of the Boltzmann map and show that it satisfies the Markov property even for sets that halt exploration mid-edge.

papers.title: On a Supersymmetric Generalization of the Matytsin Formula
papers.abstract: We derive the leading asymptotics of the supersymmetric analogue of the Itzykson-Zuber integral for the supergroup $U(n|m)$ in the limit $n,m\to\infty$ when $n/m$ is kept finite. This generalizes the Matytsin result for $U(N)$. We show that it is described by the classical action of two independent Hamiltonian systems corresponding to the bosonic and fermionic sectors.

papers.title: Reset Quantum Channels
papers.abstract: We introduce Reset Quantum Channels (RQCs), a class of quantum channels acting on a Hilbert space structured as a direct sum of an arbitrary number of subspaces. Within each subspace, the state evolves unitarily; across subspaces, it is transferred by measure-and-prepare resets along given states. In this general setting, we show that the determination of their invariant states reduces to a stochastic eigenvalue problem, whose size is set by the number of reset states rather than by the dimension of the Hilbert space, and we discuss the uniqueness of these states. We further address the primitivity and the spectrum of these channels, which we compute explicitly when the reset states commute with the unitary evolutions. Applications include a small system coupled to several thermal reservoirs. We also consider random unitary evolutions and analyze the averages of the invariant states in this setup. Finally, we show that a suitable continuous-time limit yields Lindblad generators of reset type on the algebra of block-diagonal operators.

papers.title: Moments, Equilibrium Equations and Barycentric Coordinates
papers.abstract: In a previous article, we applied the classical theory of moments to establish equilibrium equations for rather general finite systems of interacting particles. An equilibrium of such a system occurs if and only if the corresponding ``zeroth'' moment $\mu_0$ and the first moment $\mu_1$ vanish. Our focus then was on the relationship between $\mu_0$, $\mu_1$ and the second moment $\mu_2$ in order to produce systems of equilibrium equations solely dependent on mutual distances, including a generalization of the Albouy-Chenciner equations for central configurations in Celestial Mechanics. In the present work, we explore in depth the condition of simultaneously vanishing $\mu_0$ and $\mu_1$ on its own. This condition defines at once a vector space which is studied via barycentric coordinates and elementary exterior algebra, thereby yielding families of equilibrium equations for systems with any consistent number $n$ of particles and dimension $d$. As before, the present equilibrium equations are homogeneous as well as invariant by oriented isometries (for interactions depending only on mutual distances). Our method also develops and extends the approach by A. Albouy from central configurations of codimension $c=(n-1)-d$ equal to one, the so-called Dziobek configurations, to equilibria of systems of interacting particles of arbitrary codimension. Despite the similar appearance, our generalized Albouy equations constitute new equilibrium equations when $c$ is greater than one, even in the case of central configurations. The paper closes with applications to central configurations, with specific results for $n=5,6$ in dimension $d=2$.

papers.title: Dynamics of a spherical ferromagnet on a non-conducting incline in an external magnetic field
papers.abstract: Magnetic particles of various shapes and sizes are used in biomedical applications, robotics, nanomagnetism, electrotechnology, and education. Yet despite years of study, a theoretical description of the rolling motion of a solid magnetic sphere still eludes us. One of the reasons is that coupling magnetic fields with mechanical degrees of freedom creates a highly non-linear motion with non-holonomic constraints, which makes modeling these systems analytically or by simulations non-trivial. The Lagrange-d'Alembertian approach to holonomic systems remains one of the most versatile methods to prove central theorems and solve problems in analytical mechanics and electrodynamics. While non-holonomic systems are not accessible by the original theory, recent developments generalize the principle to certain dissipative systems. Here, we present a successful application of these developments to a simple mechanical system comprising a magnetic solid sphere on an incline within an external magnetic field. Using numerical simulations, we characterized how the system depends on its initial parameters. Furthermore, our findings are in line with recent experiments, demonstrating that even very weak magnetic fields can cause unexpected motion of ferromagnetic objects. The simplicity of this example also makes it a promising candidate for undergraduate physics education where the treatment of non-holonomic variational principles is still widely uncommon.

papers.title: Comparing weakly interacting and free quantum dynamics locally
papers.abstract: Lieb-Robinson bounds (LRBs) have become a standard tool for perturbative results in quantum many-body physics, including gap stability and many-body adiabatic theory. Here, we use LRBs to locally approximate weakly interacting many-body dynamics with one-body dynamics on large, perturbative time scales. This allows us to use one-body transport results to establish the expected many-body transport behavior on finite time scales in the following two illustrative settings: (i) We prove quantum diffusion, as quantified by a certain operator spreading diagnostic, in weakly interacting and weakly disordered Fermi systems in dimensions $D\geq2$ on large finite time scales based on the non-interacting diffusion result of Black, Drogin, and Hern\'andez [arXiv:2506.06468]. (ii) We show for Fermi-Hubbard models with initially low spin-down density, that all local multi-time spin-up correlation functions are approximated by their free counterparts. In particular, we obtain an OTOC (out-of-time-ordered correlator) counterpart to the patterns of short-time entanglement related to lattice path counts observed numerically by Bippus et al. [Phys. Rev. B 113, 035152 (2026)].

papers.title: Quantum Dobrushin comparison and locality of fermionic equilibrium states
papers.abstract: We prove a quantum analogue of Dobrushin's comparison theorem for lattice fermions. As in the classical case, it is a tool for proving uniqueness of equilibrium states, decay of correlations, and stability of local expectations under distant perturbations. We apply it to fermions with weak many-body interactions added to a quadratic Hamiltonian, allowing pairing, spatial inhomogeneity and long-range interactions. If the quadratic Hamiltonian is gapped, there is a coupling strength below which the thermal equilibrium (KMS) state is unique at every positive temperature and its correlations decay uniformly in the temperature. Its local expectations converge to those of the unique gapped ground state exponentially fast in the inverse temperature. In the same regime, local perturbations perturb locally in a strong sense (strong LPPL): every equilibrium state of a system with a distant defect is locally close to the equilibrium state without the defect, however strong or extended the defect is. The same holds for finite-volume Gibbs states with arbitrary even boundary terms. Without a gap, uniqueness, decay of correlations and strong LPPL hold at each positive temperature for interactions below a coupling strength that depends on the temperature. At high temperature, they hold for general interactions.

papers.title: From Giant Vortex States to Bright Solitons in Rapidly Rotating Bose--Einstein Condensates with Attractive Interactions
papers.abstract: We study the ground state of a Bose--Einstein condensate (BEC) with attractive interaction of strength $ a_\Omega $, confined by a two-dimensional anharmonic trap rotating at angular velocity $ \Omega $. We prove the occurrence of a phase transition, as $ \Omega \to\infty $, from an annular giant vortex state to an angularly localized bright soliton. More precisely, we distinguish three regimes according to the relative sizes of the radial and angular concentration scales. In the weak coupling regime $ a_\Omega = \mathcal{O}({\Omega}^{-1/2}) $, the limiting angular profile is governed by a variational problem on the unit circle showing rotational symmetry breaking: below a given sharp threshold, the condensate remains uniformly distributed in the annulus and has a giant vortex profile with a vortex-free bulk and macroscopic circulation; above it, rotational symmetry is broken. In the intermediate coupling regime $ \Omega^{-1/2} \ll a_\Omega \ll 1 $, the condensate localizes at a point on the unit circle with radial and angular widths of order $ \Omega^{-1/2} $ and $ a_\Omega \sqrt{\Omega})^{-1} $, respectively. After rescaling, the limiting profile factorizes into the ground state of the one-dimensional harmonic oscillator in the radial variable and a one-dimensional bright soliton in the angular variable. In the regime $ a_\Omega = a \in (0,a^*) $, corresponding to stable attraction below the collapse threshold $ a^* $ both the radial and angular widths are of order $ \Omega^{-1/2} $; consequently, the limiting profile is no longer a product but rather a genuinely two-dimensional localized state.

papers.title: Large deviations, effective dynamics, and dynamical phase transitions in random maps
papers.abstract: Large deviation theory provides a natural framework to characterize rare fluctuations of time-averaged observables in deterministic and stochastic systems. Building on previous results for deterministic chaotic maps, here we extend the Doob transform to random maps, constructing an effective dynamics in which rare events become typical. This makes it possible to directly reproduce the dynamics of rare trajectories that are exponentially difficult to sample under the original dynamics. We further apply spectral large-deviation methods to characterize dynamical phase transitions in random maps. The spectral structure of the tilted operator provides insight into the mechanisms underlying these transitions and, in particular, allows us to identify the appropriate initial states that select one dynamical phase or another. Our results extend the connection between large deviation theory, spectral methods, and effective dynamics to random chaotic maps, providing a general framework to study rare events and dynamical phase transitions in these systems.

papers.title: Entropy production from crossing a quantum separatrix
papers.abstract: If the Hamiltonian of a large quantum system depends on a variable parameter, its parameter-dependent energy spectrum may often form a dense lattice of avoided crossings. If the parameter slowly changes, the system's time evolution through the avoided crossings tends in the semi-classical limit to change from adiabatic to diabatic across a narrow energy range that has recently been defined as a quantum separatrix. Here we show that in the extreme semi-classical limit of a quasi-continuously dense spectrum, all quantum separatrices form a universal one-parameter family, and that evolution through the separatrix becomes efficiently ergodizing. If the unitary evolution is realistically averaged over small variations in the parameter time dependence, quantum separatrix crossing generates diagonal entropy according to a universal formula. Numerical examples confirm that the results for quasi-continuous spectra remain clearly recognizable in finite systems, with only small finite-size effects.

papers.title: A covariant analysis of massless Dirac fields in LRS spacetimes
papers.abstract: We investigate the massless Dirac field in locally rotationally symmetric (LRS) spacetimes using a covariant spinorial-fluid representation, with the spinor current and spin direction aligned with the LRS frame. When the current has both vorticity and sheet twist, characterized by a constant ratio $\lambda$, the LRS integrability condition relates evolution and propagation derivatives, reducing the field equations to an ordinary differential system that can be integrated exactly. The integrability of the chiral angle forces the heat flux to vanish and the source to saturate the null energy condition along the two radial null directions. A constant boost in the radial Lorentzian two-plane maps the spinor current to a canonical congruence, which is stationary (LRS~I) for $|\lambda|>1$ and irrotational and geodesic (LRS~III) for $|\lambda|<1$. In this frame, the local metric is reconstructed in the Goode--Wainwright--Van den Bergh canonical form. For $|\lambda|>1$ the energy density is positive, and the metric is locally isometric to the horizonless charged Taub--NUT (Brill) metric: in the polar representation, the massless Dirac field supplies a stress--energy tensor algebraically identical to that of the Brill electromagnetic field, with no Maxwell field present. For $|\lambda|<1$, the energy density is negative and the metric is the hyperbolic ($k=-1$) charged NUT metric with a formal negative squared-charge parameter, whose homogeneous slices are of LRS Bianchi type~VIII.

papers.title: Consecutive Supersymmetric Quantum Mechanical Algorithms for Resolving the Spectra of Legendre-type Differential Operators
papers.abstract: Quite comprehensive iterative algorithms based on consecutive supersymmetric quantum mechanics (SUSYQM) have been constructed heuristically, for resolving the eigenspectra of the Legendre operator and its associates parametrized in various coordinates, \emph{without receiving any input from traditional analytical methods}. On building these algorithms, the two symmetries \text{--} supersymmetry and shape invariance symmetry \text{--} hidden in these operators are brought to the fore as the only two governing principles, with the aids of the newly devised algebraic techniques such as the \emph{active supersymmetrization transformations}, \emph{momentum operator maps} as well as plain and \emph{higher-order spin matrix maps}. In view of their algebraic simplicity and elegance, high efficiency, as well as independence of traditional methods, some of these algorithms become the promising candidates to supplant the popular power series approach to the eigenspectra of Legendre-type operators.

papers.title: Gap-label bounds and optical reconstruction of Landau-subband quantum geometry
papers.abstract: We derive a magnetic gap-label lower bound on the internal quantum weight of Landau subbands that remains nonzero even when the occupied Chern number vanishes. Using the second fundamental forms of nested subbundles to decompose the quantum geometric tensor, we isolate the constraint imposed by the uniform parent curvature and show that the excess quantum weight above the bound equals twice the weaker circular transition weight. For a noninteracting parabolic band with a periodic scalar potential, Landau-level mixing preserves the integrated relative curvature while the occupied direct gap remains open. Nevertheless, uncorrected sub-cyclotron absorption need not satisfy the projected bound. Using exact circular-dipole relations, we reconstruct the low-frequency guiding-centre weight and signed dichroism from circularly polarized absorption. This reconstruction removes the first-order orbit-polarization contribution. For an insulating filling of an isolated lowest-Landau-level-derived cluster, a potential-gradient estimate bounds the omitted remote-transition weight quadratically at weak coupling. This yields a finite-window lower bound on reconstructed quantum weight and bounds the deviation of reconstructed dichroism from the integrated relative curvature.
